description:
src/lib.rs:200-214 — `Error::Aia(pkix_aia::AiaError)` carries a single
AiaError. The rustdoc says:

    Carries the underlying [`pkix_aia::AiaError`] from the last fetch
    attempt; earlier failures are dropped because the chain builder
    iterates URIs in caller-supplied order and only the final blocker
    determines the outcome.

(PKIX-q9hv.8 already notes the rustdoc is inaccurate about the
ordering reasoning — separate issue.) The contract issue here is
different: callers debugging \"why did AIA chain reassembly fail\"
see exactly ONE error, and have no way to learn:

- how many URIs were tried
- which URI produced which error
- whether failures were homogeneous (all timeout) or heterogeneous
  (some 404, some malformed)

To debug, a caller MUST wrap their `AiaFetcher` impl in a
logging/recording shim that captures all per-URI results outside
the wrapper's error channel. That's the same pattern as the
SignatureVerifier shim used in tests, but undocumented as a
debugging requirement.

Three reasonable directions:

a) Document the limitation prominently in the rustdoc for
   `Error::Aia` with a worked example of the logging-shim pattern.
   Cheapest fix; doesn't change the API.

b) Change `Error::Aia` to carry a richer payload:
       Aia { errors: Vec<(String, AiaError)> }
   Records every URI + its error so callers see the full picture.
   More allocation; useful for debug.

c) Add a third path: surface `Error::Aia` with the last error AND
   provide a `Verifier::with_aia_observer(...)` callback the verifier
   invokes per-URI for logging. Closure-based, no error-type change.

(a) is cheap and may be enough. (b) is the most caller-honest. (c) is
the most flexible but adds API surface.

This is distinct from PKIX-q9hv.8 (which is about rustdoc accuracy on
URI ordering). The contract gap here is the lossy aggregation,
independent of order.

Caller impact: anyone debugging AIA failures in production. With
n URIs and 1 error message, mean-time-to-diagnose scales with n.
title: Error::Aia carries only the last fetch error; earlier failures silently dropped
